summary: Order placement 500s are caused by the order-service v2.14.0 release (dep-5101, deployed 12:10:00Z): the newly introduced MarginCheckValidator dereferences a null marginProfile with no null guard, throwing NullPointerException on F&O orders 2 minutes after deploy and stepping order-service error_rate from ~0.20% to 18.49% at 12:12Z. All 426 errors carry the MarginCheckValidator NPE / "marginProfile is null" signature and are filtered to orderType=FNO, exactly the change's stated scope ("add margin check for F&O orders"). Competing origins are contradicted: dep-5088 predates onset by ~2h36m and only bumps gRPC, no config change touched order-service or its dependencies, and all four derivatives-adjacent peers (market-data, exchange-gateway, pricing-engine, portfolio-service) stayed flat at ~0.2% error_rate throughout, which falsifies a shared-infrastructure path and removes the only mechanism by which upstream data could be blamed. Confidence 0.85 (high), capped for the unexecuted narrow-window change confirmation and the missing order-service resource-saturation cross-check; the recommended fix is to roll back dep-5101 (or patch the validator with a null guard / explicit marginProfile loading).

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) introduced a null-marginProfile NPE in the new F&O margin validation path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v2.14.0 refactor of order-service replaced the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() with a new MarginCheckValidator. The new validator dereferences marginProfile without a null guard (or fails to populate/load it), so for F&O (derivatives) orders where marginProfile is null the validator throws NullPointerException, the request fails, and POST /v1/orders returns HTTP 500. All 426 errors are confined to orderType=FNO, exactly the order class the deploy summary says the change targets.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5101 deploys order-service v2.14.0 at 12:10Z, adding MarginCheckValidator and removing legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()
The new validator is inserted into the validation chain for F&O orders only (per deploy summary 'add margin check for F&O orders')
Two minutes later, first error at 12:12:31Z is NullPointerException in MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88) for orderType=FNO
The same class the deploy introduced is the faulting frame; 224 NPE-at-validator + 202 'marginProfile is null' errors, all filtered to FNO
Validator throws -> order-service returns 500 on POST /v1/orders -> error_rate steps from 0.20% (12:05Z) to 18.49% (12:12Z) and stays 17.9-19.0% through 13:57Z
Peer/downstream services (market-data, exchange-gateway, pricing-engine, portfolio-service) all remain flat at ~0.2% error_rate, so nothing downstream is generating this failure

assumptions: The 12:05->12:12Z step is due to the validator path and not a coincident resource exhaustion; order-service latency/pool metrics were not retrieved (gap).
No unrecorded feature-flag/infra change landed within 2 minutes of onset (change inventory possibly incomplete - gap).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Null marginProfile originates from an upstream data source (portfolio-service / ledger-db), and the new validator merely surfaces pre-existing bad data
ranked_hypotheses.statement: marginProfile is derived margin data owned downstream of order-service (portfolio-service writes ledger-db, a shared store). If that data path began returning/omitting marginProfile for F&O accounts, the newly deployed validator would NPE on data it was never defensive against. On this reading the trigger is a data_issue at the margin-data owner, not the order-service release itself.

causal_chain.claim: marginProfile is margin data not owned by order-service; portfolio-service reads/writes the shared ledger-db and is the plausible owner
portfolio-service v4.2.1 (dep-5088) deployed at 09:36Z, a gRPC bump that could alter data shape served to consumers
A missing/blank marginProfile for FNO accounts flows into order-service's validation chain (no guard in new code)
Validator dereferences null marginProfile -> NPE -> 500 for F&O orders

assumptions: portfolio-service marginProfile output actually changed and is the source of the null.
The NPE only manifests because order-service code lacks a null guard.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared datastore/middleware (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka) degraded at onset, causing order-service failures over a shared path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service inherits shared components (ledger-db, redis-cache via pricing-engine, kafka) that also serve portfolio-service. If one of these saturated or degraded around 12:10-12:22Z, order-service requests could fail. The 500s would then be a downstream/shared-infrastructure symptom rather than a local code defect.

causal_chain.claim: order-service depends on shared ledger-db, redis-cache and kafka; portfolio-service shares ledger-db and redis-cache
order-service calls fail and surface as 500 on POST /v1/orders

assumptions: A shared component actually degraded; no telemetry for ledger-db/redis-cache/kafka was retrieved.
Shared-component failure could produce a validator-level NullPointerException rather than a connection/timeout error.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Adjacent service change (cfg-2101 on notification-service / other adjacent change) rejecting derivative orders
ranked_hypotheses.statement: An adjacent change near onset — the only recorded config change, cfg-2101 on notification-service (email.batch_size 200->250 at 11:21Z) — or some other adjacent-service rollout is rejecting derivative order requests, causing order-service 500s without order-service code changing.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2101 changes notification-service email batching at 11:21Z, ~1h before onset
This change reaches order-service's F&O order path

assumptions: notification-service has a functional link to the F&O order path (no evidence for this).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: notification-service has no functional link to the order path (F16); the failure is an in-process NullPointerException in order-service's own newly deployed MarginCheckValidator (F8, F9, F15), not an external rejection; and all adjacent peers are flat (F13).

facts.statement: Dep-5101 deployed order-service v2.14.0 at 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z with summary 'Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders' and changes 'new MarginCheckValidator in validation chain' and 'remove legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()'; status live, rolled_back_at null.

The first order-service ERROR appeared at 2026-03-03T12:12:31Z — 2 minutes after dep-5101 landed — as 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88) orderType=FNO orderId=9326cc69', with 426 matching ERROR lines through 13:58:50Z.

The error signature is a null marginProfile NPE surfacing as the client-facing 500: 224 occurrences of 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(...) orderType=FNO' and 202 of 'order rejected with <n>: java.lang.NullPointerException: marginProfile is null for account <n>', both filtered to orderType=FNO.

order-service error_rate stepped between the 12:05Z and 12:12Z buckets from 0.20% to 18.49%, remaining elevated (17.93-18.97%) in every bucket through 13:57Z against a 11:30-12:05Z baseline of 0.18-0.27%.
The faulting stack frame is inside the exact class the deploy introduced, so the failing code path is the newly deployed validator rather than a pre-existing path.

No config change touched order-service or any of its dependencies in the 11:00-14:00Z window; the only change was cfg-2101 on notification-service (email.batch_size 200->250 at 11:21Z), which has no functional link to the F&O order path.

All four derivatives-adjacent peers stayed flat over the incident: market-data-service (min 0.1%, max 0.32%, 12:12Z bucket 0.22%), exchange-gateway (12:12Z bucket 0.17%), pricing-engine (12:12Z bucket 0.19%) and portfolio-service (12:12Z bucket 0.22%).

The only other deployment in the 24h window, dep-5088 to portfolio-service v4.2.1 ('bump grpc 1.62 -> 1.63'), landed at 2026-03-03T09:36:00Z — ~2h36m before onset — touches only a gRPC version, and can reach order-service only indirectly via shared ledger-db/redis-cache.

order-service inherits shared upstream paths (ledger-db shared=true, redis-cache shared=true via pricing-engine, kafka, market-data-service), so a shared-component fault could in principle produce the symptom; the flat peer error rates argue against it here.

No historical precedent matches the null-marginProfile NPE signature; the closest order-service precedents are connection-pool exhaustion (HIST-115), ledger-db IOPS throttling (HIST-110) and an external exchange outage (HIST-103), all latency/resource or timeout signatures.

assumptions: The 12:05Z -> 12:12Z step is attributable to the new validator code path and not to a coincident resource-exhaustion event: order-service latency, request_rate, cpu_pct and db_pool_in_use were not retrieved, so a resource-pressure contпоribution to the 500s is assumed absent rather than verified.

No unrecorded infrastructure-level or feature-flag change landed within ~2 minutes of onset: the change inventory (2 deployments, 1 config change over 24h) is assumed complete; an infra/cloud change feed and a feature-flag service were not queried.
The reviewed hypothesis ranking and confidences (H1 0.85, H2 0.12, H3 0.06, H4 rejected 0.03) are taken as fixed from shared state and are not re-derived here.

For H1's mechanism to produce the observed client-facing 500, the NPE thrown in MarginCheckValidator is assumed to be uncaught on the request path and translated into an HTTP 500 by order-service's error handling (the 224 'order rejected with <n>: ... marginProfile is null' lines are consistent with this but the handler itself was not inspected).

The 426 ERROR lines are assumed to be the full population of failed requests producing the ~18% error_rate elevation (the log query was truncated to 40 of 426 matches), i.e. no distinct error family is hidden in the unreturned portion.

timeline.event: dep-5088 deployed portfolio-service v4.2.1 (gRPC 1.62 -> 1.63); the only other deployment in the window, ~2h36m before onset.
cfg-2101 applied to notification-service (email.batch_size 200 -> 250) by config-bot; the only config change in the window and unrelated to the order path.
Last pre-incident bucket: order-service error_rate 0.20% avg.
dep-5101 deploys order-service v2.14.0 ('Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders'; new MarginCheckValidator, legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() removed). Status live.
order-service error_rate steps to 18.49% avg and stays elevated (17.93-18.97%) through 13:57Z; peers market-data, exchange-gateway, pricing-engine and portfolio-service remain flat ~0.2%.
First order-service ERROR: NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88), orderType=FNO, orderId=9326cc69.
Both dominant error patterns established (MarginCheckValidator NPE and 'marginProfile is null for account <n>'), all filtered to orderType=FNO; 426 matching ERROR lines total.
Incident INC-001 reported by on-call SRE: HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, order-service error-rate alert firing.
Last matching ERROR line in the observed window.
End of data window: dep-5101 still live, rolled_back_at null; error_rate still ~18% (not recovered).

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) to the last known-good release, or, if rollback is not feasible in the incident window, hotfix MarginCheckValidator to null-guard / explicitly load marginProfile before validation and redeploy.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5101 is the change that introduced the faulting class and predates the first 500 by 2 minutes; the error signature (MarginCheckValidator NPE 'marginProfile is null', orderType=FNO only) is exactly the change's stated scope, and error_rate has been stuck at ~18% with error volume flat since 12:12Z — the change is still live and the symptom is ongoing.

recommended_actions.action: Verify mitigation by confirming order-service error_rate returns to the 0.18-0.27% baseline and that MarginCheckValidator NullPointerException / 'marginProfile is null' log lines cease after the rollback or hotfix; also confirm rolled_back_at is populated for dep-5101.
recommended_actions.rationale: The elevated error_rate (18.49% step at 12:12Z, still 17.93-18.97% through 13:57Z) is the discriminating signal; confirming it recedes closes the loop on the rollback and distinguishes this failure from any residual data-side cause.

recommended_actions.action: Add a null-marginProfile guard plus explicit marginProfile population/load path in MarginCheckValidator, with F&O unit/integration coverage asserting the validator never dereferences a null profile and returns a typed business error rather than an uncaught NPE.
recommended_actions.rationale: The root cause is a missing null guard on a newly added validation path (uncaught NPE produced the client-facing 500); a typed rejection instead of a 500 is the correct product behavior for missing margin data.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument and alert on validation-path-specific error metrics for order-service (per-validator / per-orderType error counters) so a refactor-induced NPE surface is caught in the 12:05-12:12Z style step by an alert rather than by support tickets.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 0.20%->18.49% step at 12:12Z was visible in error_rate, but detection came from a support-reported spike 10 minutes later at 12:22Z; finer-grained signal shortens time-to-detect for similar local code-path failures.

recommended_actions.action: Require canary/staged rollout with mandatory rollback criteria for order-service validation and margin-path changes, and enforce a null-safety review checklist on refactors that remove legacy validators (legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() -> MarginCheckValidator).
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5101 was fully live with no rollback, and the change removed a legacy validator in favor of a new one without a null guard; staged rollout plus review gates would have contained the F&O-only blast radius.

recommended_actions.action: During the incident window, if rollback is delayed, discriminate the remaining low-confidence alternatives cheaply: query order-service latency_p99/request_rate/cpu_pct/db_pool_in_use and the shared components' (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka) health for 12:10-12:22Z; a pure code-path failure should show no local saturation. Note that a shared-component or upstream-data origin is already disfavored because market-data, exchange-gateway, pricing-engine and portfolio-service error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2%.
recommended_actions.rationale: Resource-saturation metrics for order-service and shared components were never retrieved, so H2/H3 cannot be formally closed; this check separates a pure code-path NPE from resource-pressure or shared-datastore causation without slowing the rollback of the confirmed suspect.

data_gaps: Order-service latency_p99_ms, request_rate, cpu_pct and db_pool_in_use were never retrieved — cannot confirm whether the 500s coincide with local latency/saturation (i.e. pure code-path failure vs. resource-pressure-driven).

No telemetry was queried for shared components (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka) or pricing-engine for 12:10-12:22Z, so the shared-infrastructure path (H3) cannot be formally closed by observation, only disfavored by the flat peer error rates.

portfolio-service error logs and ledger-db/user-db queries were not run (tool budget exhausted), so the origin of the null marginProfile data (H2: upstream data vs. local mapping/loading) was not inspected.

The narrowed-window config-change re-query (11:00Z-13:00Z) was not executed (budget_exhausted); the wider 24h query returned count=1 with partial=false, so an unrecorded config change on a shared component close to onset cannot be fully excluded.
Deployment/config inventory completeness is unverified: only 2 deployments and 1 config change over 24h, with no broader infra/cloud change feed or feature-flag source queried.
Dependency map is limited to depth 2 from order-service/portfolio-service; transitive owners upstream of ledger-db/kafka are not inventoried.

exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate and upstream_latency_ms were not queried, so a downstream dependency of exchange-gateway being impacted cannot be fully ruled out (only its own error_rate is known flat).

The order-service ERROR log result was truncated (40 of 426 matches returned), so per-instance/per-endpoint distribution of the 500s is unconfirmed; onset time and top patterns are reliable but not exhaustive.
No historical incident matches the null-marginProfile NPE signature, so it is unconfirmed whether this is a recurring known pattern.
Whether dep-5101 was rolled back after 13:59Z is unknown (window ends at latest data; rolled_back_at null as of 13:59Z), so mitigation effectiveness is unverified.
One tool failure (tc-011: query_metrics error_rate for pricing-service, not_found) — immaterial to the conclusion since pricing-engine error_rate was obtained via F13.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A subsequent observation that the MarginCheckValidator null guard / marginProfile loading path already existed and the NPE arose from a source other than the validator dereference (e.g. an unpopulated field injected upstream) would shift the origin toward H2 (data/source owner).

Evidence that order-service was already erroring on F&O orders before 12:10:00Z, or that error_rate was already elevated in the 12:05Z bucket, would break the deploy-to-onset causal link and reopen the alternative hypotheses.

A fast, complete recovery after some other change (e.g. an unrecorded config/feature-flag flip around 12:10-12:22Z that was reverted) rather than after rollback of dep-5101 would indicate the real trigger lay outside the deployment.

Detection of simultaneous degradation in a shared component (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka) or in pricing-engine within 12:10-12:22Z, correlated with order-service failures, would revive H3 (shared infrastructure) as the origin.

Proof that portfolio-service or ledger-db began emitting/omitting null marginProfile data for F&O accounts at or shortly before 12:10Z — with the new validator merely exposing pre-existing bad data — would make H2 the better-ranked origin.

Any indication that the errors are not confined to orderType=FNO (e.g. the truncated log sample hides non-FNO failures) would weaken the scope match between dep-5101's stated change and the blast radius.

A material resource-saturation signal on order-service (pool exhaustion, CPU saturation, latency spike) coincident with onset would suggest a resource-driven failure mode rather than the deterministic null-dereference, changing the recommended immediate mitigation toward capacity/pool remediation.

Temporal proximity makes dep-5101 the change closest to symptom onset (order-service itself, 12 min before 12:22Z), while dep-5088 (09:36Z) and cfg-2101 (11:21Z) are further from onset and touch services without a direct functional link to the F&O order path.

The error signature is a NullPointerException on a null marginProfile, surfacing as the client-facing 500: two dominant patterns cover all 426 errors -- 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:<n>) orderType=FNO' (224) and 'order rejected with <n>: java.lang.NullPointerException: marginProfile is null for account <n>' (202). Both patterns are filtered to orderType=FNO, the derivatives order type.
